Scanning is where a good negative quietly becomes a flat file. Clean
the glass first and the film second, with a blower before a cloth —
drag a cloth over a dusty negative and the scratch outlives the dust by
years.

Digital ICE handles dust well until it meets a grainy emulsion, where
it mistakes grain for a defect and smooths the picture it was meant to
save. Turn it off for those films and spot by hand.

Scan a little loose and set the black point from the blank film base,
not from the frame, or the shadows climb. A sixteen-bit scan keeps the
highlight roll-off that an eight-bit one clips. Keep the files well
away from the phone snapshots, or they will be edited like them.
